scan.summary: This is an internal daily (pre-shift) inspection log for one propane forklift, unit FL-2, at the Portland warehouse, covering September 2026 through the Sep 17 entry. It is evidence, not a program: it is judged on whether entries are complete and current, and on whether the one recorded defect was handled and closed out — federal OSHA does not actually require the examination to be written down, so the value of this log is purely as proof that the daily examinations happened. As read, it shows eleven day-shift entries, three missing weekdays inside the covered period, a horn defect on Sep 9 with no recorded repair or return-to-service, and nothing after Sep 17.
scan.freshness_note: Last entry is Sep 17, 2026 — ten days before today (2026-09-27). Either this is page 1 of a longer September log and the later pages were not supplied, or entries for Sep 18 and Sep 21–25 were not made. Ask for the complete September sheet before treating this as the current month's evidence.

gaps.title: Gap in entries: Sep 3 and Sep 4 have no line
gaps.description: The log runs Sep 1, Sep 2, then jumps to Sep 7. September 3 and 4, 2026 were a Thursday and a Friday (inferred from the calendar), so on a normal warehouse week two working days show no examination of FL-2.
gaps.fix: Confirm whether the truck was used on Sep 3 and 4. If it was, record the missed examinations as a gap in the record and re-brief operators that the sheet is filled in before the truck moves; if it was idle those days, write "not used" on the line so the blank is explained.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) (examination at least daily before being placed in service), adopted in Oregon by OAR 437-002-0220

gaps.title: Horn defect on Sep 9 with no repair or return-to-service entry
gaps.description: The Sep 9 row marks Horn as "X" with the note "Horn not working", but every other item on that row is ticked and the row is signed off; there is no entry showing the truck was taken out of service, no repair date, no who fixed it, and no return-to-service sign-off. The next line, Sep 10, simply shows all ticks.
gaps.fix: Add a defect-closeout line or an attached work order for FL-2 showing date the horn was repaired, by whom, and who released the truck back to service. Going forward, add a "Removed from service / returned by / date" box to the sheet so a defect cannot be closed silently.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) ("Defects when found shall be immediately reported and corrected") and 29 CFR 1910.178(p)(1) (truck in need of repair, defective or unsafe to be removed from service) — Oregon applies these through OAR 437-002-0220

gaps.title: Nothing recorded after Sep 17
gaps.description: The sheet ends at Sep 17. Sep 18 and Sep 21–25 were working weekdays (inferred from the calendar) with no line, so for the last ten days there is no written evidence that FL-2 was examined.
gaps.fix: Supply the rest of the September sheet if it exists; if it does not, resume entries immediately and note the interruption. Keep the month on one sheet so the run of dates is visible.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7), adopted in Oregon by OAR 437-002-0220
gaps.locator: page 1, end of table after row "Sep 17"

gaps.title: Only "Day" shift lines, while the company is recorded as running more than one shift
gaps.description: Every row on this sheet is marked "Day". The company record already carries site_operates_multiple_shifts. If FL-2 is also operated on a later shift, that shift's examination is not on this log. (Inferred — the log itself says nothing about other shifts.)
gaps.fix: Decide and write down whether FL-2 is used on any shift other than day. If it is used round the clock, add a line per shift; if it is day-shift only, note that on the sheet header so the single daily line is self-explaining.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) — per-shift examination where trucks are used on a round-the-clock basis

gaps.title: Operators identified by initials only
gaps.description: The Operator column carries "M.C." and "J.R." with no printed name or signature. As evidence, initials are weak — they cannot be tied to a named, evaluated operator without a separate key.
gaps.fix: Have operators sign or print a full name, or keep a one-line key on the sheet mapping initials to names, and cross-check both against the forklift operator training/evaluation certifications.
gaps.citation: No rule requires a written inspection record at all (see OSHA interpretation, 9 May 2000); this is a record-quality point, not a rule breach.

deadlines.source_line: Inspection per OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7): examine before each shift; do not use if a defect affects safety.

LPG fuelling brings cylinder storage and exchange requirements and fire-code storage limits on top of the forklift rules.

facts.value: 4,886 hours (Sep 17, 2026); 4,812 at the start of the month

facts.value: Two operators recorded by initials: M.C. and J.R.

facts.affects: Both need current training and a three-yearly evaluation on file under 1910.178(l); ties to certified_forklift_operators and forklift_operator_evaluation_due_dates.

facts.value: Day shift only on this log

Confirms LPG cylinders are exchanged on site — cylinder handling, storage location and operator training on cylinder change are in scope.

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence on what the page shows: header, truck, month, the eleven dated rows, hour meter figures, the Sep 9 horn "X" with "Horn not working", and the Sep 15 "Tank changed" note are all legible in the photo. High confidence that federal 1910.178 applies in Oregon through Oregon OSHA's adoption by reference (OAR 437-002-0220, with additional Oregon rules at OAR 437-002-0227) — I checked that; I have not read the full Oregon subdivision text, so I cannot say whether any Oregon addition touches daily examination specifically. High confidence that no rule requires the examination to be written at all — OSHA has said so in interpretation letters — so every finding above is about the quality of voluntary evidence, not a breach of a record-keeping rule. Medium confidence on the day-of-week reasoning behind the Sep 3, 4 and 18 findings: that is calendar arithmetic, marked inferred, and the truck may simply have been idle. I cannot tell from one page whether more September pages exist or whether the horn was repaired before the truck was used again.
